coverage: Schematic connectivity re-derived from native symbol/pin geometry in inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_sch (J1 rotated 180 deg at 60.96,63.5; R1 at 86.36,63.5; C1 at 101.6,63.5) and cross-checked against work/netlist/design.xml and work/netlist/connectivity.json: /IN={J1.1,R1.1}, /OUT={R1.2,C1.1,J1.2}, GND={C1.2,J1.3} all confirmed.

PCB copper connectivity traced segment-by-segment in inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_pcb: /IN track J1.1-R1.1, /OUT tracks R1.2-C1.1 plus J1.2 stub landing mid-segment at (107.5,100), GND track C1.2 to via (113,100) into B.Cu zone; zone filled_polygon inspected and thermal-relief spokes around J1.3 at (100,105.08) confirmed present; /IN and /OUT pads confirmed isolated from the GND zone by the fill cutout.

Geometry requirement (min 0.2 mm) independently verified against the raw board file: all five segment entries carry (width 0.25); zone min_thickness 0.25 mm; via 0.6 mm/0.3 mm drill is not a track segment; consistent with work/geometry/geometry.json.

ERC and DRC records (work/erc/erc.json, work/drc/drc.json) reviewed including ignored-check lists; zero violations, zero unconnected items, zero parity issues consistent with my manual netlist/layout trace.
Board outline fit: all footprint courtyards, the via, and the zone polygon verified inside the 20x12 mm Edge.Cuts rectangle (96-116, 96-108).

findings.condition: The only copper path from C1.2/the GND track to J1 pad 3 is: F.Cu track (110.95,100)-(113,100) -> single via (0.6 mm, 0.3 mm drill) -> B.Cu GND zone -> thermal-relief spokes into J1.3 at (100,105.08). There is no redundant GND track.

findings.location: inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_pcb (via uuid b71a70d7-bbc1-43d1-ae55-5e4d992412a4 at 113,100; zone uuid 38a83012-bcf9-4bb9-b9f4-50d49cd91d90)
findings.mechanism: If the zone were refilled under different rules, or the single via were compromised in fabrication, the GND net would open and the filter would lose its return path. The packet itself notes the fill is evaluated only as saved and a refill pass is forbidden, so this single dependency is exactly the part of the connectivity with the weakest evidence chain.
findings.reasoning: I verified the thermal spokes exist in the saved filled_polygon and DRC reports zero unconnected items, so the net is connected as saved and this is not a defect. It is recorded as an info-level concern because GND continuity rests on a single via plus a fill state that the toolchain is forbidden from regenerating; for a disposable review fixture this is acceptable, but it is the one connection not corroborated by any explicit track.
findings.title: GND return to J1.3 depends entirely on the saved zone fill and a single 0.3 mm-drill via

findings.condition: The geometry probe run emitted three instances of 'assert "m_choices.GetCount() > 0" failed in PROPERTY_ENUM(): No enum choices defined' from pcbnew internals alongside its normal output.

evidence.locator: tracks[] five segment entries each width_mm 0.25; counts 3 footprints / 6 track items / 1 zone

findings.mechanism: Non-fatal assertion failures inside the measuring tool raise the possibility of partially initialized tool state producing unreliable measurements, even though the process exited 0.
findings.reasoning: I cross-checked every number the probe reported (segment count, widths, pad positions, via, zone) against the raw native board file and they all match, so the measurement outcome is trustworthy and the geometry pass verdict stands. The assertion spam is tool noise worth flagging so the operator knows the probe's environment is slightly degraded, not a defect in the candidate.
findings.title: Geometry probe console contains repeated internal KiCad assertion failures

limitations: work/rc-step/result.raw is binary and was not inspectable; waveform shape between measurement points is taken from the .meas results and ngspice.log only.

Zone copper continuity is assessed from the saved filled_polygon coordinates and KiCad's own connectivity check; no refill or independent polygon-geometry computation was possible (read-only candidate, no tools).
Per the declared scope, component tolerance, temperature, external loading, ADC sampling, EMI, ampacity, and manufactured-hardware behavior were not evaluated.
Tool executions could not be re-run; exit codes, hashes, and logs were accepted as recorded after internal consistency checks.
The vout_1ms measurement is taken at absolute t=1 ms while the stimulus completes at t=1 ns; the ~1 ppm timing mismatch versus '1 ms after the step' is negligible and was not raised as a finding.
